segments.text: the aim of launch Readiness is simple
make sure the entire organization is
ready to market sell deliver and support
our product at a level that achieves our
launch objectives
checklist of launch deliverables are
certainly helpful but they only tell
part of the story plus they typically
are generalized lists copied from other
websites
that miss things that are essential to
your organization
they also become bloated over time as
more deliverables get added to the quote
unquote checklist
everybody seems to have their favorite
the four dimensions of launch Readiness
are business
Marketing sales and product
the business Dimension ensures the
everyday aspects of our product are in
place so that we can conduct business
it's easy to assume things like
accepting payment are simple and it can
be addressed with an email or a quick
phone call
but we often underestimate how
complicated these things can be for the
people who actually do them
the marketing Dimension is about
choosing the best target market segments
who or who's our Focus who are we going
to go after
we also know that our product is a good
fit for those market segments and we
have a message that resonates with
Buyers plus a demand gen engine in place
to fill a sales pipeline
the sales Dimension focuses on the
activities required to help the sales
team understand why buyers need our
product
they can qualify a sales opportunity
they can nurture that sales opportunity
to a close they know the pricing and
discounting structure they'll get paid
for selling our product we can pay them
commission and know where to get sales
help when they need it on a deal by deal
basis
the product Dimension ensures our
product can be delivered to customers
they can be onboarded efficiently they
become successful when using our product
and help is available when they need it
a launch Readiness checklist helps you
evaluate the state of launch Readiness
not whether the deliverables are ready
or not but whether the organization is
ready
the difference between our launch
checklist and most others is ours
focuses on the capabilities you need for
a successful launch each capability is
designed to provoke the question how
will we do that which in turn leads to a
discussion of what activities and what
deliverables are needed for the
capability to be a reality here we see
an example that focuses on the sales
team
one of the first questions is
can our sales people communicate our
unique value proposition to our
prospects
can our salespeople identify and qualify
a good sales opportunity
the implication by this is can they also
identify a bad one and know when to walk
away
can our sales people guide prospects
from interest to intent to purchase
if you find a capability on the launch
Readiness checklist that doesn't apply
to your product launch just remove it
add the capabilities you need but always
resist the urge to turn it into a long
list of deliverables you can download
the launch Readiness checklist from the
BrainCraft members file share area or by
using the link below schedule some time
with us to discuss how to use the launch
Readiness checklist
or discuss any product launch concerns
you have
we look forward to hearing from you
